# EARS: Explanatory Abstention for Reliable Sub-Agent Modeling in Large-scale Multi-Agent Systems

## Thesis
A framework that trains specialized sub-agents to detect their own limitations and return structured failure explanations to a central coordinator, improving system reliability.

## Topic
Sub topic: Multi-Agent Systems; LLM Calibration; Abstention Modeling; Production AI Systems. Primary focus: Sub-agent reliability; Inter-agent communication protocols; LLM-as-a-Judge calibration; Supervised fine-tuning for failure detection

## Problem
Problem statement: In centralized multi-agent systems, smaller specialized sub-agents often over-answer ambiguous, unsupported, or misrouted requests, producing hallucinated outputs instead of actionable feedback for the coordinator.. Why it matters: Reliability of large-scale enterprise MAS depends on sub-agent execution, not just coordinator routing. Prior work focuses on top-down routing, leaving sub-agent communication breakdowns and execution failures unexplored. Over-answering by sub-agents propagates errors to end-users and wastes computational resources.

## Key novelty
Main idea: Explanatory Abstention for Reliable Sub-Agent Modeling (EARS). Explanation: Reframes abstention from a final user-facing refusal into a structured inter-agent communication signal.; Uses an ensemble of calibrated LLM judges to automatically curate high-precision abstention labels from production data.; Fine-tunes sub-agents to output category-specific failure rationales that enable coordinator-level clarification or rerouting.

## Problem definition
Formal setting: Centralized MAS with a coordinator routing queries to domain-specialized sub-agents. The goal is to improve sub-agent response reliability by detecting unsolvable queries and returning structured abstention signals.. Inputs: User query, sub-agent context, available capabilities and business constraints.. Outputs: Task-specific structured response (e.g., DSL query) OR structured abstention signal containing a failure category and rationale.

## Key terms
Explanatory Abstention: A sub-agent's practice of detecting its own capability limits and returning a categorized failure reason to the coordinator.. LLM-as-a-Judge Calibration: Iteratively refining prompt instructions for an LLM evaluator using human-annotated data to improve its accuracy in classifying failure modes.. Abstention Taxonomy: A set of mutually exclusive failure categories: Ambiguous Query, Insufficient Input, Missing Capability, and Misrouting.

## Related work
Sub area: MAS Routing & Orchestration. What it does: Focuses on coordinator-level strategies to route queries to specialists based on knowledge boundaries and cost-performance trade-offs.. Open gap: Neglects sub-agent execution failures and the lack of communication signals between sub-agents and coordinators.. Citations: RIRS; MasRouter | Sub area: Model Abstention & Refusal. What it does: Studies when single-agent models should refuse unanswerable questions using RL-based post-training or answerability gating.. Open gap: Treats abstention as a terminal user-facing refusal rather than a coordination signal within a multi-agent workflow.. Citations: Abstain-R1; LatentRefusal

## Method
High level flow: Offline Calibration: Human annotation -> LLM judge calibration -> Data curation; Online Flywheel: Judge ensemble curation -> Sub-agent SFT -> Deployment -> New interaction data. Modules: Module: Abstention Taxonomy & Human Annotation. Role: Defines failure categories and creates a high-quality seed dataset via hierarchical dual-annotation.. Model: None (human process). Inputs: Raw human-agent interaction samples. Outputs: Annotated seed dataset with category labels and rationales. Notes: Uses independent dual-annotation with adjudication to resolve disagreements. | Module: LLM-as-a-Judge Calibration. Role: Optimizes judge prompt instructions to accurately classify abstention categories on the seed set.. Model: LLM (e.g., Gemini, Claude, GPT). Inputs: Seed dataset; Initial prompt. Outputs: Calibrated judge prompt. Notes: Iterative human-in-the-loop revision until accuracy threshold is met. | Module: Ensemble Data Curation. Role: Applies calibrated judges to large-scale production data to generate training labels.. Model: Ensemble of 3+ LLMs (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini). Inputs: Production interaction logs; Calibrated prompts. Outputs: Curated abstention-aware training dataset. Notes: Uses unanimous agreement for high precision; threshold is tunable. | Module: Sub-Agent Fine-Tuning. Role: Trains the domain-specialized sub-agent to recognize failure conditions and output structured abstention signals.. Model: Qwen3-32B-Instruct. Inputs: Curated dataset (queries, context, expected responses). Outputs: Fine-tuned sub-agent model. Notes: Full-parameter SFT with AdamW, cosine LR schedule, 3 epochs.. Novel architectural elements: Reframes sub-agent output space to include structured abstention signals as first-class coordination payloads.; Closes a data flywheel where deployed sub-agents generate new interaction data that feeds back into the judge curation pipeline.. Design choices: Unanimous judge agreement to maximize label precision and prevent converting answerable queries into abstention cases.; Hierarchical annotation process to minimize ambiguity and guide logical label decisions.; Full-parameter fine-tuning instead of parameter-efficient methods to capture nuanced abstention boundaries across multiple categories.

## Model details
Base model: Qwen3-32B-Instruct. Training: Method: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Objective functions: Purpose: Minimize cross-entropy loss on task-specific outputs and structured abstention signals. Formally: Standard next-token prediction loss over curated instruction-response pairs.. Adaptation: Full-parameter fine-tuning. Key hyperparameters: Optimizer: AdamW. Learning rate: 1e-5 (peak, cosine schedule). Warmup ratio: 5%. Epochs: 3. Batch size: 8. Max seq length: 32768

## Comparison to prior work
Related methods: RIRS: Routes agents based on knowledge boundaries and planning.; MasRouter: Unified decision problem for collaboration modes and LLM selection.; Abstain-R1: RL-based post-training for single-agent abstention.; LatentRefusal: Answerability gating for Text-to-SQL.. Key differences: vs. Routing methods: Focuses on sub-agent execution reliability and inter-agent communication rather than coordinator routing.; vs. Single-agent abstention: Treats abstention as a structured coordination signal for downstream recovery, not a terminal user refusal.

## Proposed evaluation
Evaluation setting: Production e-commerce business intelligence assistant handling customer segmentation and analytics queries.. Benchmarks: Name: Production e-commerce interaction dataset. Task type: Text-to-DSL generation & abstention classification. Newly constructed: True. Baselines: Incumbent MAS without abstention training; Single-judge curation variants; Human-annotated only curation. Main metrics: Overall Pass Rate (Syntax Validity + Semantic Correctness); Abstention Ability (Accuracy, Precision, Recall); Computational Cost (normalized token usage). Ablations: Effect of abstention data vs. raw production data; Human-annotated seed vs. LLM-curated data; Single-judge vs. multi-judge consensus curation

## Falsifiable predictions
Pillar: Explanatory Abstention as Coordination Signal. Prediction: Sub-agents trained with structured abstention rationales will reduce hallucinated outputs on ambiguous or unsupported queries compared to baseline sub-agents.. Kill condition: Abstention training does not improve pass rate or semantic correctness on ambiguous/unsupported queries, or degrades performance on solvable queries. | Pillar: Ensemble Judge Curation. Prediction: Unanimous multi-judge agreement will yield higher-precision training labels and better sub-agent performance than single-judge curation.. Kill condition: Multi-judge consensus shows no improvement or worse performance than single-judge curation due to excessive label filtering. | Pillar: Data Flywheel Continuity. Prediction: Iteratively redeploying fine-tuned sub-agents and recurating data will sustain or improve response reliability over time.. Kill condition: Performance plateaus or degrades after the first fine-tuning cycle, indicating label noise or distribution shift breaks the flywheel.

## Limitations
Domain-adaptive design evaluated only on e-commerce BI workflows, requiring validation in other sectors.; Relies on human-in-the-loop calibration for LLM judges, limiting full automation scalability.; Does not optimize coordinator-level recovery policies or routing adjustments following sub-agent abstention signals.; Unanimous judge agreement prioritizes precision over recall, potentially missing valid abstention cases for human review.

# MOSAIC: Composable Safety Alignment with Modular Control Tokens

## Thesis
A framework that uses learnable control tokens to dynamically activate and combine safety rules without modifying the base model.

## Topic
Sub topic: Large Language Model Safety; Conditional Alignment; Token-based Control. Primary focus: Modular constraint activation; Compositional control tokens; Over-refusal mitigation

## Problem
Problem statement: Current safety alignment methods either entangle safety rules in model weights or rely on weak natural language prompts, making it hard to dynamically apply different safety policies for different users or contexts.. Why it matters: Safety standards vary across regions, age groups, and applications, requiring flexible conditional control. Retraining models for each policy is costly and risks degrading general capabilities. Prompt-based methods lack reliable enforcement and scale poorly with multiple constraints.

## Key novelty
Main idea: MOSAIC. Explanation: Encodes each safety rule as a small set of learnable embedding tokens prepended to inputs.; Composes multiple safety rules at inference time by concatenating their corresponding tokens.; Trains tokens jointly using order-based sampling and counterfactual distillation to prevent over-refusal.

## Problem definition
Formal setting: Given a frozen LLM f_θ and a set of safety categories C = {c_1, ..., c_K}, the task is to condition the model's generation on an active subset of categories S ⊆ C.. Inputs: User instruction x and an active subset of safety categories S.. Outputs: Model response conditioned on the active safety categories S and input x.

## Key terms
Control Tokens: Learnable embedding vectors that represent specific safety constraints and are prepended to inputs to steer model behavior.. Order-based Task Sampling: A training strategy that allocates fixed data budgets per number of active constraints to efficiently cover combinatorial token combinations.. Counterfactual Knowledge Distillation: An objective that aligns the model's output distribution with control tokens to its original distribution without tokens on benign inputs to reduce over-refusal.

## Related work
Sub area: Safety Alignment. What it does: Uses post-training methods like SFT, RLHF, and preference optimization to embed safety directly into model weights.. Open gap: Entangles safety with general capabilities, making updates costly and risking catastrophic interference.. Citations: citation | Sub area: Pluralistic Alignment. What it does: Adapts LLMs to diverse values using meta-instructions, specialized community models, or controllable alignment prompts.. Open gap: Focuses on value preferences rather than conditional safety refusal, lacking mechanisms for combinatorial safety control.. Citations: citation

## Method
High level flow: Token Initialization -> Compositional Task Sampling -> Joint Optimization -> Inference Composition. Modules: Module: Control Token Embeddings. Role: Represent safety constraints as learnable vectors. Model: Learnable embeddings in model's input space. Inputs: Safety category index. Outputs: Token embeddings z_c. Notes: Only trainable parameters; backbone remains frozen | Module: Compositional Sampler. Role: Generate training subsets of categories. Model: Order-based allocation strategy. Inputs: Set of categories C. Outputs: Ordered subsets T_r. Notes: Allocates fixed budget per order to prevent exponential data growth | Module: Training Objective. Role: Optimize tokens for refusal and utility preservation. Model: Cross-entropy and KL-divergence losses. Inputs: Instructions, active tokens, labels. Outputs: Optimized token embeddings. Notes: Uses counterfactual KD for negative samples. Novel architectural elements: Control tokens are prepended to the input sequence rather than injected into model layers.; Multiple constraint tokens are concatenated linearly to compose policies.; Backbone model parameters remain completely frozen during training.. Design choices: Freezing the backbone preserves general utility and avoids catastrophic interference.; Order-based sampling prevents exponential data growth while ensuring tokens learn cooperative interactions.; Counterfactual KD uses the frozen model as a teacher to align benign responses, reducing over-refusal without extra labeled data.. Theoretical grounding: Frames safety alignment as a compositional representation learning problem where control tokens act as modular constraint carriers in the embedding space, decoupling policy activation from parameter modification.

## Model details
Base model: Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.2-3B. Training: Method: Supervised fine-tuning of control tokens with counterfactual knowledge distillation. Objective functions: Positive samples: Standard autoregressive cross-entropy loss to induce refusal behavior.; Negative samples: Combined language modeling loss and KL-divergence between controlled and base model distributions to preserve benign behavior.. Adaptation: Training only control token embeddings. Key hyperparameters: Learning rate: 0.01. Epochs: 8. Kd weight: 1.0. Max output length: 256

## Comparison to prior work
Related methods: In-context prompting: Uses natural language system instructions to encode safety rules.; ORPO: Parameter-efficient alignment using LoRA and odds ratio preference optimization.; SFT with LoRA: Standard supervised fine-tuning mapping unsafe prompts to refusals.. Key differences: vs. In-context: Uses explicit learnable embeddings instead of probabilistic natural language instructions.; vs. ORPO/SFT: Keeps backbone frozen and uses modular tokens instead of updating model weights, enabling composition without retraining.

## Proposed evaluation
Evaluation setting: Conditional safety activation on already-aligned LLMs using a newly constructed benchmark of context-sensitive requests that are not rejected by default.. Benchmarks: Name: Custom 5-category safety dataset (addiction, alcohol, betting, horror, sex). Task type: Conditional refusal generation. Newly constructed: True. Baselines: In-context prompting; ORPO; SFT with LoRA. Main metrics: Defense Success Rate (DSR); Over-Refusal Rate (OR); General utility preservation. Ablations: Removing multi-task joint optimization; Removing counterfactual KD objective; Varying negative-to-positive sample ratios; Varying number of control tokens per category; Incremental category expansion

## Falsifiable predictions
Pillar: Compositional Token Activation. Prediction: Tokens will maintain high refusal rates when combined across multiple categories.. Kill condition: Significant drop in refusal performance when activating 2+ categories simultaneously. | Pillar: Counterfactual KD. Prediction: Over-refusal on benign queries will decrease compared to standard SFT.. Kill condition: Over-refusal rates remain equal to or higher than SFT baselines. | Pillar: Frozen Backbone Utility. Prediction: General language modeling capabilities will remain intact after token training.. Kill condition: Measurable degradation on unrelated general-purpose tasks.

## Limitations
Limited evaluation scale due to hardware constraints on larger models.; Dataset size is relatively small due to intensive manual filtering requirements.; May not capture the full breadth of open-domain safety edge cases.; Relies on a judge LLM for automated evaluation, which introduces potential bias.

# TABED: Test-Time Adaptive Ensemble Drafting for Robust Speculative Decoding in LVLMs

## Thesis
A training-free method that dynamically combines multiple draft models during inference to maintain consistent speedups across diverse visual and textual inputs.

## Topic
Sub topic: Speculative Decoding; Large Vision-Language Models; Inference Acceleration; Test-Time Adaptation. Primary focus: Drafting methods for LVLMs; Dynamic ensemble learning; Training-free inference acceleration

## Problem
Problem statement: Existing speculative decoding drafting methods for Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) exhibit scenario-specific performance fluctuations, making it difficult to select a single drafting approach that consistently accelerates inference across diverse multimodal inputs.. Why it matters: LVLMs require significantly higher inference time due to image token processing, making acceleration critical for real-world deployment. Current drafting methods either ignore visual context or require additional training, failing to adapt to varying turn-taking, task types, and out-of-distribution scenarios.

## Key novelty
Main idea: Test-time Adaptive Batched Ensemble Drafting (TABED). Explanation: Dynamically ensembles multiple draft predictions using batch inference without requiring separate model weights.; Adjusts ensemble weights at test time based on past deviations from the target model's verified outputs.; Maintains negligible computational overhead through parameter sharing and plug-and-play compatibility with existing verification techniques.

## Problem definition
Formal setting: Given a target model $M_p$ and a draft model $M_q$, speculative decoding generates draft tokens using $M_q$ and verifies them in parallel using $M_p$ to approximate the target distribution $p(y|x, y_{<t})$ while accelerating inference.. Inputs: Image and text prompts, past verified tokens, and target model probabilities. Outputs: Draft token probabilities and accepted draft tokens for accelerated generation

## Key terms
Speculative Decoding: An inference acceleration technique where a small draft model generates tokens that a larger target model verifies in parallel.. Drafting Method: The strategy used by the draft model to generate candidate tokens, which can be multimodal or text-only.. Block Efficiency: The expected number of accepted draft tokens per verification block.. Test-Time Adaptation: Adjusting model behavior or parameters during inference based on incoming data without retraining.

## Related work
Sub area: Speculative Decoding for LVLMs. What it does: Prior works explore text-only drafting using only the LLM component or vision-aware drafting that compresses image tokens and requires dedicated training.. Open gap: These methods either lack visual awareness or require training, and neither consistently handles diverse real-world multimodal scenarios without performance fluctuations.. Citations: citation | Sub area: Test-time Adaptation. What it does: Updates models via gradient steps using pseudo-labels or self-supervision during inference to handle distribution shifts.. Open gap: Incurs high adaptation costs and delays, unlike the ground-truth access available during speculative decoding verification.. Citations: citation

## Method
High level flow: Drafting: Batch inference with multiple drafting methods -> Weight Selection: Compute ensemble weights based on past target deviations -> Ensembling: Weighted average of draft distributions -> Sampling: Generate next draft token. Modules: Module: Batched Drafting. Role: Generates multiple draft predictions simultaneously. Model: Shared draft model M_q (e.g., LLaMA). Inputs: Batch of prefixes for different drafting methods. Outputs: List of draft distributions. Notes: Uses parameter sharing to keep costs negligible | Module: Adaptive Weight Selector. Role: Dynamically assigns weights to each drafting method. Model: Rule-based optimization. Inputs: Past target probabilities; Past draft probabilities; Weight sampling policy. Outputs: Optimal weight vector w_t^*. Notes: Minimizes KL divergence or maximizes token matches over a sliding window | Module: Ensemble Sampler. Role: Combines draft distributions and samples the next token. Model: Weighted averaging. Inputs: Draft distributions; Optimal weights. Outputs: Ensembled distribution; Sampled draft token. Notes: Continues drafting until block length is reached. Novel architectural elements: Dynamic test-time weight adaptation using past verification signals; Parameter-shared batched inference for multiple drafting strategies; Plug-and-play integration with token-tree verification and alternative drafting candidates. Pseudocode: Algorithm 1: TABED
Input: Batch b_<t, block length, weight sampling policy S_W
1. Sample weight list W_t from S_W(t)
2. Select w_t^* by minimizing distance D(p_t', q_t'^j) over past window
3. For i from 0 to block length-1:
   a. Obtain distributions [q^(1)_t+i, ..., q^(m)_t+i] from M_q(b_<t+i)
   b. Compute ensembled q_t+i via weighted average using w_t^*
   c. Sample y_t+i from q_t+i
4. Return draft tokens and ensembled probabilities. Design choices: Use KL divergence or token match counting for weight selection to align draft with target distribution; Cache past distributions and labels to avoid redundant computation; Employ sliding window for adaptation to capture recent context shifts. Theoretical grounding: Ensemble learning reduces bias and variance; adaptive weighting ensures the ensembled distribution closely approximates the target model's output distribution, preserving speculative decoding's theoretical guarantees.

## Model details
Base model: LLaMA-68M or LLaMA-160M (draft), LLaVA-1.5-7B/13B or LLaVA-NeXT (target). Training: Method: Training-free inference adaptation. Objective functions: Purpose: Align draft distribution with target distribution. Formally: Minimize KL divergence D_KL(p(y_t'|x, y_<t'), q(y_t'|x, y_<t'; w_t)) over past steps. Adaptation: Test-time dynamic weight adjustment. Key hyperparameters: Block length: 5. Window size h: variable. Weight sampling policy: S_W

## Comparison to prior work
Related methods: Multimodal Drafting (M): Uses full image and text inputs for drafting; Text-only Drafting (T): Uses only text inputs for drafting; Static Ensemble: Fixed equal weights for combining drafts. Key differences: vs. M/T: Dynamically adapts to scenario shifts instead of relying on a single fixed strategy; vs. Static Ensemble: Adjusts weights based on real-time performance deviations rather than fixed averages

## Proposed evaluation
Evaluation setting: Multi-turn instruction interactions across diverse benchmark and out-of-distribution datasets, evaluating block efficiency and walltime speedup.. Benchmarks: Name: LLaVA-W, DocVQA, POPE, MMVet, IEdit, MB, Spot. Task type: Visual question answering, document understanding, reasoning. Newly constructed: False | Name: PSV, VIST. Task type: Out-of-distribution multi-image queries. Newly constructed: False | Name: NQ, GSM8K. Task type: Text-only reasoning and QA. Newly constructed: False. Baselines: Multimodal Drafting (M); Text-only Drafting (T); Static Ensemble (StaticMT); Random Ensemble (RandomMT). Main metrics: Block efficiency; Expected walltime speedup; Draft-to-target latency ratio. Ablations: Replace dynamic weights with static equal weights; Replace dynamic weights with random weights; Vary weight sampling policies and window sizes; Compare KL divergence vs. Total Variation Distance for weight selection

## Falsifiable predictions
Pillar: Dynamic Weight Adaptation. Prediction: TABED will consistently achieve higher block efficiency than static or single drafting methods across diverse input scenarios.. Kill condition: Static or single drafting methods match or exceed TABED's performance across all tested scenarios. | Pillar: Training-Free Efficiency. Prediction: Ensembling multiple drafts via parameter sharing will maintain negligible computational overhead compared to single drafting.. Kill condition: The batched ensemble inference introduces significant latency that negates speedup gains. | Pillar: OOD Robustness. Prediction: Dynamic weighting will effectively down-weight underperforming methods in out-of-distribution scenarios, maintaining robust speedups.. Kill condition: Performance degrades significantly on OOD datasets compared to benchmark datasets.

## Limitations
Primarily evaluated on LLaVA series models; generalization to other LVLM families like Qwen-VL or LLaMA 3.2 requires further validation.; Experiments limited to small-capacity draft models; scaling to billion-parameter draft models remains unexplored.; Lacks a rigorous theoretical framework connecting the past time-step window size to optimal dynamic weight selection.; Plug-and-play compatibility assumes standard speculative decoding pipelines; integration with non-standard architectures may require modifications.

title: Strategy Executability in Mathematical Reasoning: Leveraging Human-Model Differences for Effective Guidance
intuition: Main idea: Selective Strategy Retrieval (SSR). Explanation: Treats strategy effectiveness as model-dependent, selecting hints that a specific model can actually operationalize rather than just copying successful examples.; Combines human and model strategies by recognizing their complementary strengths in structural versus procedural reasoning tasks.; Uses a multi-path retrieval system to gather diverse evidence, ensuring robust guidance even when direct performance signals are sparse.

# Strategy Executability in Mathematical Reasoning: Leveraging Human-Model Differences for Effective Guidance

## Thesis
The framework improves mathematical reasoning by selecting inference-time guidance based on whether a target model can actually execute the strategy, rather than just copying successful examples.

## Topic
Sub topic: Mathematical Reasoning; Inference-Time Guidance; Large Language Models. Primary focus: Strategy executability; Human-model strategy differences; Test-time strategy retrieval

## Problem
Problem statement: Example-based guidance for mathematical reasoning is highly unstable because strategies that appear in successful solutions are not always executable by a target model when transferred as guidance.. Why it matters: Guidance reliability is crucial for improving LLM mathematical reasoning without expensive training. Prior work conflates strategy usage with executability, ignoring systematic human-model differences that cause guidance failures.

## Key novelty
Main idea: Selective Strategy Retrieval (SSR). Explanation: Treats strategy effectiveness as model-dependent, selecting hints that a specific model can actually operationalize rather than just copying successful examples.; Combines human and model strategies by recognizing their complementary strengths in structural versus procedural reasoning tasks.; Uses a multi-path retrieval system to gather diverse evidence, ensuring robust guidance even when direct performance signals are sparse.

## Problem definition
Formal setting: Given a problem x, a target model m, and a prompting/decoding protocol π, executability is defined as U(s|x; m, π) = P(success=1 | x, s, m, π), the probability that strategy s leads to a correct solution.. Inputs: A mathematical problem and a set of candidate reasoning strategies extracted from human or model solutions.. Outputs: A ranked subset of strategies selected as inference-time guidance for the target model.

## Key terms
Strategy Usage: How frequently a reasoning strategy appears in successful solutions.. Strategy Executability: Whether a strategy remains effective when instantiated as guidance for a target model under fixed inference conditions.. Selective Strategy Retrieval (SSR): A test-time framework that selects strategies based on empirical executability signals rather than usage frequency or semantic similarity.

## Related work
Sub area: Inference-Time Reasoning Guidance. What it does: Uses worked examples, reasoning traces, or hints to steer model generation during inference.. Open gap: Assumes guidance is universally transferable based on semantic similarity or correctness, ignoring model-specific executability.. Citations: citation | Sub area: Reasoning Traces and Strategy Abstraction. What it does: Represents solutions as step-by-step traces or higher-level plans for supervision or routing.. Open gap: Focuses on trace faithfulness or plan selection without analyzing whether strategies remain executable across different models or contexts.. Citations: citation

## Method
High level flow: Strategy Knowledge Graph Construction -> Problem Representation -> Multi-Route Strategy Retrieval -> Executability Prediction & Ranking -> Guidance Generation. Modules: Module: Strategy Knowledge Graph. Role: Organizes reasoning knowledge into a heterogeneous graph of problems, strategies, and categories to propagate executability signals.. Model: Heterogeneous graph neural network with transformer-style message passing.. Inputs: Paired human/model solutions and extracted strategies from HM-ReasoningBench. Outputs: Structure-aware node embeddings encoding executability patterns. Notes: Trained with a contrastive objective separating successful from unsuccessful problem-strategy pairings. | Module: Multi-Route Strategy Retrieval. Role: Retrieves candidate strategies via three complementary routes to form an over-complete candidate set.. Model: Temperature-scaled softmax aggregation over semantic neighbors and graph embeddings.. Inputs: Problem embedding h_x and graph embeddings. Outputs: Candidate strategy set S(x). Notes: Routes include category-conditioned, problem-transfer, and semantic fallback retrieval. | Module: Executability Predictor. Role: Estimates the utility of each candidate strategy for the target model.. Model: Parametric estimator using logistic function on aggregated features.. Inputs: Problem-strategy feature representation φ(x,s). Outputs: Calibrated executability probability Ũ_θ(s|x). Notes: Trained with negative log-likelihood on trial-level supervision; uses Beta-Binomial model for empirical scores.. Novel architectural elements: Multi-route retrieval combining category, transfer, and semantic signals.; Source-aware retention in the knowledge graph to handle human-model strategy divergence.; Separation of structure-aware representation learning from supervised executability prediction.. Design choices: Using empirical executability signals instead of usage frequency to avoid unreliable proxies.; Multi-route retrieval to ensure coverage and capture different levels of executability evidence.; Source-aware retention to leverage complementary strengths of human and model strategies.. Theoretical grounding: Executability is formalized as a model-relative, protocol-relative probability. Empirical estimation uses a Beta-Binomial model to account for decoding stochasticity, providing a calibrated posterior mean for strategy success probability.

## Model details
Base model: Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B (target models); pretrained sentence encoder; heterogeneous graph neural network. Training: Method: Supervised fine-tuning for executability predictor; contrastive learning for graph embeddings. Objective functions: Contrastive loss for graph embeddings to separate successful/unsuccessful pairings.; Negative log-likelihood for executability predictor to approximate true success probability.. Adaptation: No adaptation to target LLMs; purely test-time framework.. Key hyperparameters: Temperature: 0.7. Max context: 32768. Decoding trials: T independent trials for supervision

## Comparison to prior work
Related methods: Direct Solving (DS): Baseline without guidance.; In-Context Learning (ICL): Provides one worked example.; Human-Only/Model-Only Guidance (H/M): Uses strategies from a single source.; Self-Consistency, Least-to-Most, Tree-of-Thoughts: Stronger inference-time baselines using sampling/search.. Key differences: vs. ICL/H/M: SSR explicitly models executability and combines multi-source strategies rather than relying on semantic similarity or single-source hints.; vs. SC/L2M/ToT: SSR achieves gains with a single guided generation per problem, avoiding extensive test-time computation.

## Proposed evaluation
Evaluation setting: Mathematical reasoning benchmarks requiring multi-step symbolic and structural reasoning, evaluated with exact-match accuracy and proof verification.. Benchmarks: Name: HM-ReasoningBench. Task type: Mathematical reasoning (algebra, geometry, number theory, combinatorics). Newly constructed: True | Name: AIME 2025. Task type: Competition-level mathematical reasoning. Newly constructed: False | Name: MathArena Apex. Task type: Extreme difficulty final-answer mathematical reasoning. Newly constructed: False. Baselines: Direct Solving; In-Context Learning; Human-Only Guidance; Model-Only Guidance; Self-Consistency; Least-to-Most Prompting; Tree-of-Thoughts. Main metrics: Exact-match accuracy; Output token consumption; Strategy adherence rate. Ablations: Removing category-conditioned retrieval route.; Removing problem-transfer retrieval route.; Removing semantic fallback retrieval route.; Analyzing gains by problem topic and failure mode.

## Falsifiable predictions
Pillar: Strategy Executability Modeling. Prediction: Selecting strategies based on empirical executability signals will consistently outperform selection based on usage frequency or semantic similarity across diverse mathematical domains.. Kill condition: SSR performs no better than random strategy selection or single-source guidance across multiple benchmarks. | Pillar: Human-Model Strategy Complementarity. Prediction: Human-derived strategies will yield larger guidance gains for problems requiring global structural decomposition, while model-derived strategies will excel for procedural tasks.. Kill condition: Human and model strategies show no systematic domain-dependent performance differences when used as guidance. | Pillar: Multi-Route Retrieval Necessity. Prediction: Each retrieval route contributes uniquely to executability estimation, and removing any route degrades performance.. Kill condition: A single retrieval route matches or exceeds the full multi-route system's performance.

## Limitations
Requires a curated dataset of paired human and model solutions to construct the strategy knowledge graph and train the predictor.; Executability estimation depends on the specific target model and decoding protocol, requiring re-calibration for different models.; Strategy extraction relies on prompting pipelines and rule-based matching, which may miss novel or highly specific reasoning patterns.; The framework adds computational overhead for embedding, graph lookup, and strategy ranking at test time.

title: Same Signal, Opposite Meaning: Direction-Informed Adaptive Learning for LLM Agents
intuition: Main idea: DIAL (Direction-Informed Adaptive Learning). Explanation: Models state uncertainty as a mixture of decision-difficult states where rollouts help and intervention-unsuitable states where they hurt.; Collects signal-agnostic counterfactual data via randomized exploration to avoid selection bias from fixed-direction priors.; Fits a sparse linear gate over universal and LLM-proposed features to learn the utility direction per environment and backbone.

# Same Signal, Opposite Meaning: Direction-Informed Adaptive Learning for LLM Agents

## Thesis
A learned sparse gate adapts to when extra computation helps or hurts LLM agents by discovering how uncertainty signals relate to task outcomes in each environment.

## Topic
Sub topic: Adaptive test-time compute; LLM agents; Uncertainty estimation; Gating mechanisms. Primary focus: Learning signal-utility direction; Counterfactual exploration; Sparse linear gating

## Problem
Problem statement: Existing adaptive compute gates assume a fixed relationship between uncertainty signals and the value of extra computation, but this relationship reverses across environments and model backbones, causing gates to actively select harmful states.. Why it matters: Wastes compute resources by triggering rollouts when they degrade performance. Fixed-direction gates fail across heterogeneous agent settings due to unstable signal semantics. There is a lack of principled methods to align gating signals with actual counterfactual utility.

## Key novelty
Main idea: DIAL (Direction-Informed Adaptive Learning). Explanation: Models state uncertainty as a mixture of decision-difficult states where rollouts help and intervention-unsuitable states where they hurt.; Collects signal-agnostic counterfactual data via randomized exploration to avoid selection bias from fixed-direction priors.; Fits a sparse linear gate over universal and LLM-proposed features to learn the utility direction per environment and backbone.

## Problem definition
Formal setting: At each step t, an agent observes state s_t and selects action a_t. An optimizer T can be invoked. The utility is U(T, s) = E[R(a=T(s))] - E[R(a=π(s))]. The goal is to learn a gate g: S -> {0,1} that triggers T only when U > 0.. Inputs: State s_t and gating signal φ(s_t) (e.g., entropy). Outputs: Binary gate decision g(s) ∈ {0, 1}

## Key terms
Fixed-direction assumption: The prior assumption that higher uncertainty or difficulty always indicates greater value for additional computation.. Two-source model: A decomposition of states into Type I (intervention-unsuitable, negative signal-utility slope) and Type D (decision-difficult, positive signal-utility slope).. Utility calibration: Aligning gating signals with the counterfactual value of additional computation, rather than just action correctness.. Signal-agnostic exploration: Collecting training data by randomly triggering the optimizer, independent of any uncertainty signal, to avoid selection bias.

## Method
High level flow: Explore: Signal-agnostic data collection -> Reason: Feature construction -> Learn: Sparse linear gate fitting. Modules: Module: Explore. Role: Collects paired counterfactual outcomes (state, utility) without conditioning on gating signals.. Model: Bernoulli trigger with probability p_explore. Inputs: State s_t; Base policy action; Optimizer action. Outputs: Dataset D of (φ(s_t), U_t) pairs. Notes: Forks environment to run truncated rollouts for both base and optimizer actions. | Module: Reason. Role: Constructs a candidate feature pool combining universal features and LLM-proposed task-specific features.. Model: LLM prompt for feature hypothesis generation. Inputs: Summary of exploration dataset D. Outputs: Candidate feature pool φ_cand(s). Notes: Universal features include step_count, token_entropy, evidence_count, etc. LLM proposes 5 task-specific features. | Module: Learn. Role: Fits a sparse logistic regression gate to predict optimizer utility.. Model: L1-regularized logistic regression. Inputs: Dataset D; Candidate features φ_cand(s). Outputs: Deployed gate g(s) with weights w* and bias b*. Notes: L1 penalty performs feature selection and direction discovery. Threshold set by cross-validation.. Novel architectural elements: Signal-agnostic Bernoulli exploration to eliminate selection bias; Two-layer feature pool (universal + LLM-proposed) with L1 sparsity for automatic feature selection; Signed weight diagnostic to interpret per-environment signal-utility direction. Pseudocode: Input: Environment E, agent policy π, optimizer T, universal features φ_univ, LLM M, budget N_explore, rate p_explore, threshold τ
Output: Deployed gate g
// Phase 1: Explore
D ← ∅
for episode = 1 to N_explore:
    Run π in E; at each step t, invoke T with prob p_explore independent of state
    Record (s_t, U_t) pairs into D
// Phase 2: Reason
(p_E, H) ← M(summary(D))
φ_cand ← φ_univ ∪ extract(H)
Recompute φ_cand(s) for all s ∈ D
// Phase 3: Learn
Standardize φ_cand on D
Select C via 5-fold CV on held-out log-loss
Fit L1-regularized logistic regression: w*, b* = argmin Σ L(w^φ(s)+b, U) + (1/C)||w||_1
Keep features with non-zero w_i*
g(s) ← 1[sigmoid(w*^T φ(s) + b*) > τ]
return g. Design choices: L1 regularization over L2 to enforce exact sparsity and enable signed-weight diagnostics; Signal-agnostic exploration to prevent baking fixed-direction priors into training data; Binarizing continuous utility for logistic fitting to preserve sign direction; Universal features defaulting to zero for missing signals to avoid per-environment engineering. Theoretical grounding: Two-source model decomposes marginal signal-utility correlation as a weighted blend of Type I (negative slope) and Type D (positive slope) regimes. Demonstrates that uncertainty alone is insufficient for VOC (Value of Computation) and that direction reversal is a structural consequence of Simpson's paradox across (environment, backbone) pairs.

## Model details
Base model: Qwen3-4B-Instruct, Phi-3.5-mini-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Training: Method: Supervised learning on counterfactual utility labels. Objective functions: Purpose: Predict binary optimizer utility. Formally: Binary cross-entropy loss L(w, b) + (1/C)||w||_1. Adaptation: L1-regularized logistic regression (LASSO). Key hyperparameters: P explore: 0.5. N explore: 50. C: selected via 5-fold CV over [0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1.0, 3.0, 10.0]. Threshold: 0.5

## Comparison to prior work
Related methods: CaTS: Calibrated confidence gating; SEAG: Mean token confidence search allocation; CoRefine: Conv1D confidence controller; CATTS: Vote entropy + margin arbiter; AUQ: Verbalized uncertainty reflection; s1_budget: Fixed token budget. Key differences: vs. CaTS/SEAG/CoRefine: Learns direction from data instead of assuming low confidence always needs more compute; vs. CATTS: Zero per-step LLM overhead after one-time exploration vs K=5 forward passes; vs. AUQ: Uses signal-agnostic exploration to avoid selection bias vs verbalized uncertainty triggers

## Falsifiable predictions
Pillar: Two-Source Model (Temporal Dynamics). Prediction: Signal-utility correlation should decrease over the episode as information accumulates and late-step uncertainty reflects residual intervention-unsuitable states.. Kill condition: Correlation increases or remains constant from early to late steps across multiple environments. | Pillar: Two-Source Model (Causal Manipulation). Prediction: Restricting evidence (increasing Type I mixture) will make step_count dominant with negative correlation, while injecting gold evidence will make entropy dominant with positive correlation.. Kill condition: Information manipulation does not shift the dominant signal identity or its correlation sign as predicted. | Pillar: Signal Insufficiency. Prediction: No single uncertainty signal can reliably predict optimizer utility across all environments and backbones; direction will reverse.. Kill condition: A single signal (e.g., entropy) maintains a consistent positive correlation with utility across all tested environments and backbones.

## Limitations
FEVER is the weakest setting where useful rollouts concentrate in early steps that random exploration may miss.; Incurs a one-time exploration cost per (environment, backbone) pair before deployment.; Excludes end-to-end RL gating controllers, which could confound direction attribution.; Truncation horizon H in utility estimation introduces approximation bias relative to full-episode returns.; Online adaptation mode may trigger harmful rollouts in Type-I-dominant environments during ε-greedy exploration.
